answer.worked:
Place vertical asymptotes at the two zeros of $f$. Between them, $f(x)>0$, so the reciprocal rises to $+\infty$ beside both asymptotes. The maximum $(0,\frac32)$ becomes the minimum $(0,\frac23)$. Outside the zeros, $f(x)<0$, so the reciprocal falls to $-\infty$ beside the asymptotes. As $x\to\pm\infty$, $f(x)\to-\frac12$ from above, so the reciprocal approaches $y=-2$ from below. Thus $-2$ is excluded and $\frac23$ is included:
$$R=(-\infty,-2)\cup\left[\frac23,\infty\right).$$
